name: Souskluitjies
summary: Dumplings in cinnamon syrup: light spoon dumplings poached until puffed, then drenched in a buttery cinnamon-sugar syrup.
about: Souskluitjies — “sauce dumplings” — are an old Afrikaans winter pudding with Dutch roots: little spoon dumplings poached in water, then soaked in a cinnamon-sugar syrup made from the cooking liquid. Made from pantry staples, they are a thrifty farmhouse dessert for a cold evening.
steps: Bring the water to the boil with a pinch of salt in a wide pot that has a tight lid. Mix the cinnamon sugar and set it aside.
Sift the flour, baking powder and salt into a bowl and rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like fine crumbs.
Whisk the eggs and milk together and stir them into the flour to make a thick, smooth batter that drops from a spoon in a blob.

Turn the water down to a steady simmer. Dip a tablespoon in the hot water, then drop in spoonfuls of batter, 8–10 at a time, leaving room for them to double. Cover tightly and simmer for 8–10 minutes without lifting the lid, until puffed and a skewer comes out clean.
Lift the dumplings into a warm serving dish with a slotted spoon, sprinkling cinnamon sugar between the layers. Cook the rest of the batter the same way.

For the syrup, pour off all but 500 ml of the cooking water. Add the sugar, butter, cinnamon stick and ground cinnamon and boil over medium-high heat for 8–10 minutes, until syrupy and reduced by about a third.
Pour the hot syrup over the dumplings and serve straight away, with custard if you like.
